subject: SIEM delivery proofing & log/trace handoff for FinoSys audit
messages:
From: ops-admin@finosys.com (Ravi Shah)
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: audits@finosys.com, security-eng@finosys.com
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIEM delivery proofing request — logs, traces, and custody artifacts

Hi Neha,

We have a scheduled audit in three weeks and the compliance team needs a short self-contained handoff package showing how Redwood's private deployment will deliver observability artifacts to our Splunk instance and supply custody proof for the time range 2028-10-01 -> 2028-10-31. Specifically they asked for:
- Exact log formats (syslog/HEC JSON), examples of event JSON with field mappings
- Trace span export sample and the trace correlation key you populate
- Proof-of-delivery evidence (ingest receipts or SHA256 checksums per file/batch)
- Retention/forwarding proof for VPC deployments and on-prem forwarder behavior (eg. when the forwarder buffers and retry policy)

Can you share a minimal packet (runbook + sample logs + signed receipt) we can attach to the audit? We prefer a single PDF/spec plus any small YAML runbook snippets.

Thanks — Ravi
Ravi Shah
SRE Lead, FinoSys
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: ops-admin@finosys.com (Ravi Shah)
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, audits@finosys.com
Date: Fri, 9 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SIEM delivery proofing request — logs, traces, and custody artifacts

Hi Ravi —

Thanks for the checklist. I've attached a focused delivery spec PDF (redwood-obsv-delivery-spec-20281109.pdf) and a small runbook fragment (splunk-hec-runbook-params.yml) that together should cover the items you listed. Summary below:

1) Formats and field mapping
- Primary transport: Splunk HEC over mTLS (TLS client auth). We emit HEC JSON with top-level fields: time, host, source, sourcetype, event (object).
- Event schema: {"seq": <monotonic int>, "trace_id": "<hex>", "span_id": "<hex>", "env": "<string>", "model": "<model-name>", "lat_ms": <int>, "msg": "<string>"}
- Mapping: sample JSONs included in PDF (page 3) showing token-cost and latency fields we add for observability.

2) Tracing and correlation
- We populate trace_id as an incoming request header (x-redwood-trace) when present. If absent, we generate a v4 hex trace id and attach it to all logs and spans for that request. Span export uses OTLP->HEC bridge (server side) with "trace_key" set to trace_id. Example spans included in the PDF.

3) Proof-of-delivery
- Our forwarder returns an ingest-receipt object for each batch containing: batch_id, sha256(batch_payload), record_count, first_seq, last_seq, and timestamp. We persist receipts locally for 90 days and can provide signed receipts (HMAC-SHA256) for audit. The PDF includes a sample signed receipt and verification steps.

4) Buffering & retry behavior (VPC/on‑prem)
- On VPC: forwarder streams to HEC and uses adaptive windowing; on transient failures it will buffer in encrypted local spool (AES-256) and retry with exponential backoff up to 48 hours; after that the operator receives an alert and we provide a sequence-of-events export.
- On on-prem forwarder: same spool semantics, but customers can configure retention and retention encryption keys. We include the runbook snippet showing the config parameters (max_spool_mb, retry_policy: {initial, max_interval, max_retries}).

Next steps: I can produce a signed receipt bundle for the October window by EOD if you grant an S3/secure-share link or accept the zipped bundle via our secure upload URL. Which do you prefer?

>I attached: redwood-obsv-delivery-spec-20281109.pdf, splunk-hec-runbook-params.yml

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Manager, Customer Observability
Redwood Inference
From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: SIEM delivery proofing request — logs, traces, and custody artifacts

Ravi / team — quick operational notes to supplement Neha's packet:

- Attached runbook fragment (splunk-hec-runbook-params.yml) includes the Splunk HEC token rotation plan and the local spool encryption key rotation cadence. For audits, we normally include the token issuance ledger and a rotation log snippet (can redact token values).
- For the signed receipts: we'll generate an export with per-batch SHA256 and an HMAC signature using our key id rk-03. The verification steps: 1) compute SHA256(payload) 2) verify HMAC(signature, receipt_body, rk-03-public.pem). We can also provide the chain-of-custody log showing when the file left the forwarder and when HEC acknowledged.
- Trace retention: default 30 days in forwarder cache, full traces forwarded to customer HEC; sampling rules are configurable (by default we keep 100% of error traces, 5% of successful inference traces).

Operational question for FinoSys: do you want us to include the raw batch payloads (gzipped) with the receipts, or only receipts + sample payloads? Raw payloads increase bundle size and require an approved transfer method.

Kimberly Park
Principal Engineering Manager, Observability
Redwood Inference
